checked_scope: The CRRA compensation formula, its aggregation weights, and the zero-benefit welfare derivative on an interior equilibrium branch.
checks: For p=1−γ≠0, compensated utility derivative Sx^(p−1)>0 and its equation is Sx^p=T; positive finite solutions exist exactly for T>0, even when p<0.
Summing household utility equalities gives power-mean weights proportional to ωᵢSᵢ, with factors between individual extrema; the separately derived logarithmic case gives geometric aggregation.

Differentiating the balanced insurance budget and using the individual effort first-order condition yields (1−p)(u′U−u′E)+(τ+b)u′E p′. At b=τ=0 the fiscal term vanishes and the first is positive for interior employment and positive wage; the result remains conditional on a differentiable interior branch.
